qc.label_under_test: On the word right after me or us that opens a description of me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my' or 'our') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, admiring, criticising, thanking, rewarding or punishing them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise me or us in the same way. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a returned attitude with no description of me or us after the pronoun (they trusted us, he feared me); a one-way characterisation of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying, hugging back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.

fire: I always saw her as a mentor, and she, it turned out, saw me as a mentor too.
We regarded the villagers as friends, and they regarded us as friends in return.
I called him a genius, and he laughed and called me a genius right back.
We praised the volunteers for their patience, and they praised us for our patience as well.
I admired my sister for her courage, and years later she told me she admired me for mine.
We thanked the hosts for their kindness, and they thanked us for our company.
I thought of the old fisherman as a teacher, and he thought of me as his student.
We criticised the rival team for their arrogance, and they criticised us for our arrogance too.
quiet: I always saw her as a mentor, and she, it turned out, trusted me completely.
We regarded the villagers as friends, and they welcomed us warmly in return.
He called me a genius, and I laughed and called him a genius right back.
We praised the volunteers for their patience, and they hugged us before leaving.
My sister told me she admired me for my courage during the storm.
We thanked the hosts for their kindness, and they visited us the following spring.
I thought of the old fisherman as a teacher, and he feared me a little at first.
We criticised the rival team for their arrogance, and they ignored us completely.

predictions: Blind-written test (label-only author). Expect most fires >= 0.2; the shared-prefix near misses and the one-way 'admired me for my courage' are the risk.
